title: Problem Overview
content:
**Erdos Problem #197**

Can N be partitioned into two sets, each of which can be permuted to avoid monotone 3-term arithmetic progressions?

**Key Results:**
- The answer is YES if three sets are allowed (Erdos-Graham)
- The two-set case remains OPEN
- Cannot be resolved by finite computation

**References:**
- [ErGr79] and [ErGr80]: Erdos and Graham's foundational work
mathContext: A monotone 3-AP in a sequence f is a triple i < j < k where f(i) + f(k) = 2*f(j). This is stronger than just containing an AP as a set.
prerequisites: Bijections and enumerations of infinite sets

title: Arithmetic Progression Predicate
content:
**isArithmeticProgression:**

Three natural numbers a, b, c form an arithmetic progression if the middle one is the average of the other two.

**Definition:**
```lean
def isArithmeticProgression (a b c : N) : Prop := a + c = 2 * b
```

**Examples:**
- (1, 3, 5): 1 + 5 = 6 = 2 * 3 (YES)
- (1, 2, 4): 1 + 4 = 5 != 4 = 2 * 2 (NO)
mathContext: Three values $a, b, c$ satisfy $a + c = 2b$ iff they form an arithmetic progression with common difference $d = b - a = c - b$. Equivalently, $b$ is the arithmetic mean of $a$ and $c$.

title: Monotone 3-AP Detection
content:
**hasMonotone3AP:**

A sequence f : N -> N contains a monotone 3-AP if there exist indices i < j < k such that f(i), f(j), f(k) form an arithmetic progression.

```lean
def hasMonotone3AP (f : N -> N) : Prop :=
  exists i j k, i < j and j < k and isArithmeticProgression (f i) (f j) (f k)
```

The ordering constraint i < j < k is crucial - we care about the sequential structure.
mathContext: The predicate $\exists\, i < j < k,\; f(i) + f(k) = 2f(j)$ detects arithmetic progressions that respect the index ordering. This is strictly stronger than the set $\{f(n)\}$ containing a 3-AP, because rearranging terms can break the monotone condition.

title: 3-AP Free Sequence
content:
**avoids3AP:**

A sequence avoids monotone 3-APs if it has no such triple.

```lean
def avoids3AP (f : N -> N) : Prop := not hasMonotone3AP f
```

This is the property we want for each partition part.
mathContext: A sequence $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is 3-AP-free when $\nexists\, i < j < k,\; f(i) + f(k) = 2f(j)$. By Roth's theorem, any 3-AP-free subset of $\{1, \ldots, N\}$ has density $o(1)$, so such sequences must be sparse.

title: Enumeration of a Set
content:
**isEnumeration:**

An enumeration of a set S is a bijection from N to S.

```lean
def isEnumeration (S : Set N) (f : N -> N) : Prop :=
  Function.Bijective f and forall n, f n in S
```

This allows us to 'order' the elements of S.
mathContext: An enumeration $f : \mathbb{N} \twoheadrightarrow S$ is a bijection with $\operatorname{ran}(f) = S$. Since $S \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is infinite, such an $f$ exists by the Cantor-Bernstein theorem; the question is whether one can be chosen to avoid monotone 3-APs.

title: Set Permutable to 3-AP-Free
content:
**canPermuteTo3APFree:**

A set S can be permuted to avoid 3-APs if there exists an enumeration of S that has no monotone 3-AP.

```lean
def canPermuteTo3APFree (S : Set N) : Prop :=
  exists f, isEnumeration S f and avoids3AP f
```

This is the key property each partition part must have.
mathContext: The predicate $\exists\, f : \mathbb{N} \xrightarrow{\sim} S,\; \text{avoids3AP}(f)$ asks whether the elements of $S$ can be listed as $s_0, s_1, s_2, \ldots$ with no $i < j < k$ satisfying $s_i + s_k = 2s_j$. This is an existential statement over all possible orderings.

title: Two-Set Partition of N
content:
**isTwoPartition:**

A and B form a partition of N if they are disjoint and their union is N.

```lean
def isTwoPartition (A B : Set N) : Prop :=
  Disjoint A B and A union B = Set.univ
```

This captures the classical notion of a partition into two parts.
mathContext: A 2-coloring of $\mathbb{N}$: $A \cap B = \varnothing$ and $A \cup B = \mathbb{N}$. Equivalently, $B = A^c$. Every element belongs to exactly one of the two parts.

title: Partition Membership
content:
**partition_mem_iff:**

In a two-partition, each element belongs to exactly one part.

```lean
theorem partition_mem_iff (A B : Set N) (h : isTwoPartition A B) (n : N) :
    (n in A and n not in B) or (n not in A and n in B)
```

This is a basic but important property of partitions.
mathContext: From $A \cap B = \varnothing$ and $A \cup B = \mathbb{N}$, for each $n \in \mathbb{N}$ exactly one of $n \in A$ or $n \in B$ holds. The proof proceeds by case analysis on $n \in A \cup B$, using disjointness to rule out joint membership.

title: Erdos Problem #197 (Open)
content:
**erdos_197_conjecture:**

The main open question: Does there exist a partition of N into two sets A and B such that both can be permuted to avoid monotone 3-APs?

```lean
axiom erdos_197_conjecture :
    (exists A B, isTwoPartition A B and
      canPermuteTo3APFree A and canPermuteTo3APFree B) or
    (forall A B, isTwoPartition A B ->
      not canPermuteTo3APFree A or not canPermuteTo3APFree B)
```

Axiomatized as the disjunction of the two possible answers (yes or no).
mathContext: This formulation captures that the problem is open - we assert one of the two answers holds without knowing which.
relatedConcepts: Open problems in combinatorial number theory

title: Three-Set Partition of N
content:
**isThreePartition:**

A, B, C form a partition of N if they are pairwise disjoint and cover N.

```lean
def isThreePartition (A B C : Set N) : Prop :=
  Disjoint A B and Disjoint B C and Disjoint A C and A union B union C = Set.univ
```
mathContext: A 3-coloring of $\mathbb{N}$: three pairwise disjoint sets $A \cap B = B \cap C = A \cap C = \varnothing$ with $A \cup B \cup C = \mathbb{N}$. This is the setting where Erdos-Graham proved that 3-AP avoidance is achievable.

title: Erdos-Graham Three-Set Theorem
content:
**erdos_graham_three_sets:**

N CAN be partitioned into THREE sets, each permutable to avoid monotone 3-APs.

```lean
axiom erdos_graham_three_sets :
    exists A B C, isThreePartition A B C and
      canPermuteTo3APFree A and canPermuteTo3APFree B and canPermuteTo3APFree C
```

This proves the threshold is at most 3. The open question is whether it's 2 or 3.
mathContext: The construction uses sophisticated combinatorial techniques. The jump from 2 to 3 represents a fundamental structural change.

title: Identity Has 3-APs
content:
**identity_has_3AP:**

The sequence 0, 1, 2, 3, ... has a 3-AP at any three consecutive terms.

```lean
theorem identity_has_3AP : hasMonotone3AP id := by
  use 0, 1, 2
  ...
```

**Verification:** 0 + 2 = 2 = 2 * 1.

The natural ordering fails spectacularly!
mathContext: The identity $f(n) = n$ witnesses $(0, 1, 2)$ as a monotone 3-AP since $f(0) + f(2) = 0 + 2 = 2 = 2 \cdot 1 = 2 f(1)$. In fact any three consecutive values $n, n+1, n+2$ form a 3-AP, so the natural ordering is maximally bad.

title: Powers of 2 Avoid 3-APs
content:
**powers_of_2_avoid_3AP:**

The sequence 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, ... avoids 3-APs.

```lean
axiom powers_of_2_avoid_3AP : avoids3AP (fun n => 2 ^ n)
```

**Why:** If 2^a + 2^c = 2 * 2^b, then by uniqueness of binary representation, we need a = b = c (contradiction for a < b < c).

This is a canonical example of a 3-AP-free sequence.
mathContext: Powers of 2 have unique binary representations, which prevents the AP equality from holding with distinct exponents.

title: Non-Computability
content:
**erdos_197_not_finite_checkable:**

The two-set version cannot be resolved by finite computation.

Any finite portion of N can be partitioned to avoid 3-APs in both parts, but this doesn't guarantee a solution for all of N.

This is why the problem remains open despite decades of study.
mathContext: Compactness arguments fail here. Local solutions don't compose into global solutions.
prerequisites: Distinction between finite and infinite verification

title: Stanley Sequence
content:
**isStanleySequence:**

The Stanley Sequence S(0,1) is the 3-AP-free sequence starting with 0, 1 and greedily adding the smallest number that doesn't create a 3-AP.

**Begins:** 0, 1, 3, 5, 9, 11, 13, 15, 25, 27, ...

By construction, this sequence avoids all 3-APs.
mathContext: Stanley sequences are important in combinatorial number theory. Their density and structure are actively studied.

title: Problem Status
content:
**erdos_197_status:**

Summary of what we know:
1. The three-set version is solvable (erdos_graham_three_sets)
2. Individual 3-AP-free sequences exist (powers_of_2_avoid_3AP)

```lean
theorem erdos_197_status :
    (exists A B C, isThreePartition A B C and ...) and
    (exists f, avoids3AP f)
```

The open question is whether two sets suffice.
mathContext: The conjunction $(\exists\, A,B,C,\; \text{isThreePartition}(A,B,C) \wedge \ldots) \wedge (\exists\, f,\; \text{avoids3AP}(f))$ encapsulates two known facts: the Erdos-Graham three-set result and the existence of 3-AP-free sequences such as $2^n$.

title: The Main Open Question
content:
**erdos_197_open_question:**

Whether two sets suffice remains unknown.

```lean
theorem erdos_197_open_question :
    (exists A B, isTwoPartition A B and
      canPermuteTo3APFree A and canPermuteTo3APFree B) or
    (forall A B, isTwoPartition A B ->
      not canPermuteTo3APFree A or not canPermuteTo3APFree B) :=
  erdos_197_conjecture
```

This directly exposes the open nature of the problem.
mathContext: This theorem is a direct application of erdos_197_conjecture (proved via excluded middle). It restates the open problem: either $\exists$ a valid 2-partition, or $\forall$ 2-partitions at least one part cannot be permuted to avoid 3-APs.
relatedConcepts: Excluded middle in constructive vs. classical logic
